parsed.explanation: Combined regime imposes Tier-1 universal exposures: national binary-sex passport and entry-screening rules, federal and state birth-sex facility bans including prisons/dormitories/shelters, and birth-sex custody with documented conversion practices, forced labour and sexual abuse in immigration custody. No execution or general trans criminalisation, and courts have enjoined some orders with pending challenges, so consequences are exclusion, humiliation, detention and service denial rather than certain imprisonment. State adds no statewide gender-identity protection and a qualified-immunity religious-refusal law permitting service denial, while 15 cities offer partial cover. Minors face care bans and outing/prosecution risks. This is materially below working-protection anchors, above routine-detention/no-remedy anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex rule; X passports unavailable for new issues though existing valid; border cable directs refusal where documents/records discrepancy or reasonable doubt, and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility if wilful misrepresentation suspected. Passports confiscated/blocked reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, not automatic, limited waivers; passport policy challenged by civil-liberties suit and Supreme Court allowed restrictions to take effect.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can lead to refusal/return and, if characterised as misrepresentation, lifetime immigration consequences, interacting with state ID rules that may not match.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National prisons adopt conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormones removed, psychiatric drugs; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Facility handcuff/trespass arrest example in another state shows custody by birth sex.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Rescinded earlier prison LGBTQ order is an exposure, not protection; no documented operative remedy for custody placement in dossier. Courts enjoin some national orders generally.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facility, border or fraud allegation can move traveller into birth-sex custody where documented harm, not identity-based release, is the operative risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal binary definition bars government single-sex facilities congruent with identity; March 2025 state law defines woman/man binarily, no third category, covering bathrooms, locker rooms, shelters, rape-crisis centres, dormitories and prisons. State listed in worst-law group.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some states/cities have no ban and 15 cities bar discrimination, but state statute itself provides no gender-identity protection; map enumeration for this state via 404 page is not independently reverified.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal rule governs federal buildings/national facilities regardless of city protections; state rule governs state buildings and settings listed, creating layered birth-sex access across journey.

care_services.exposure: State bans puberty blockers/hormones/surgery for minors except severe dysphoria by two physicians; national orders restrict minor care, funding and student-loan forgiveness, hospital subpoenas for under-19 records. Adult public-insurance exclusion litigated after 2026 appellate reversal.
care_services.protection: Adult care not banned outright in dossier; pending challenge unresolved. No documented visitor-specific care-continuity protection.
care_services.interaction: Traveller needing hormones faces detention/custody removal risk nationally and insurance/referral uncertainty locally; minor traveller faces outright state restriction.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; justice memo uses 'radical gender ideology' in extremism context. State religious-refusal statute permits denial of business, housing and government service on gender identity with qualified immunity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Federal hate-crime law covers gender identity; 2020 employment ruling protects employment; several executive orders blocked/enjoined; counterterrorism text says not for mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing plus qualified-immunity refusals weakens recourse where law itself authorises denial; federal protections do not cancel state-authorized service refusal.

minors_guardians.exposure: State athletics ban by birth biology (litigated, unsettled), minor care ban, passed-but-unresolved school outing bill; national order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition including pronouns/names, funding revocation.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. Student-outing bill final status not documented; athletics ban struck by appeals court but Supreme Court agreed to hear case, operative position unsettled.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian/minor traveller can face school disclosure, sports exclusion, care denial and parental/school reporting interactions beyond adult facility exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific visitor violence rate, arrest under March 2025 state facilities statute, or refusal under religious-refusal statute is documented; absence is not safety. National poll shows majority support birth-sex document laws, indicating hostile climate for identity documents.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute, city ordinances in 15 cities, and functioning courts/litigation provide partial recourse; no documented pattern of police targeting visitors in this state.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: In cities with ordinances, local protection may mitigate street/service friction, but state religious-refusal immunity and facility law override in covered settings.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies are slow, contested and uneven: passport, executive-order, insurance and athletics challenges unresolved; state nullification of local ordinances passed Senate but house outcome not documented; facility-ban map page unavailable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, injunctions of several orders, legal-aid FAQ, city protections and federal employment/hate-crime law are documented partial remedies, not shown to prevent facility/border/custody exposure.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation may change rules during travel but cannot be relied on at a checkpoint, restroom, ward or custody intake.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal exclusion and weak remedy at borders/facilities, but this case is higher than 0.35 because fraud ineligibility is not automatic, existing X passports remain valid, courts have enjoined some orders, and no routine visitor arrest/expulsion system is documented for this state.

Lower than 0.55-C: that anchor is mainly ward placement by document with partial care denial and working complaint routes. Here birth-sex facility bans extend across bathrooms, shelters, dormitories and prisons, plus border refusal, custody abuse and legally authorized service denial.

Materially lower than 0.65-A, where national equality law guaranteed release, apology and compensation after a brief hold. Here operative federal/state rules mandate birth-sex treatment, state law gives no gender-identity protection, and remedies do not restore congruent access.

Similar to 0.45-D in durable exposure through registration/documents and administrative interviews without credible execution/imprisonment. This case is slightly lower because custody sexual abuse, forced labour and conversion practices add severity if detention occurs.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is document/presentation discrepancy leading to border refusal or facility exclusion, then possible birth-sex detention/custody where documented abuse and care removal occur. Local city protections and federal litigation mitigate some employment, hate-crime and policy issues but do not pre-empt federal entry/facilities, state facility law, or qualified-immunity service refusals. No lethal campaign is documented, keeping the score above severe-risk anchors; Tier-1 universal exposure with thin effective remedy keeps it in elevated risk.
